clinical_category: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control

semantic_correction.stem: A mechanically ventilated adult has no contraindication to semirecumbent positioning. Which nursing action is consistent with current acute-care VAP-prevention guidance?

options.A: Elevate the head of the bed to approximately 30–45 degrees as part of the prevention plan.
options.B: Keep the client routinely supine because head-of-bed elevation increases VAP risk.
options.C: Begin head-of-bed elevation after VAP is diagnosed rather than using positioning preventively.
options.D: Use head-of-bed elevation as a replacement for the rest of the ventilator-prevention strategy.

semantic_correction.rationale: The current SHEA/IDSA/APIC acute-care prevention guidance lists elevation of the head of the bed to 30–45 degrees as an essential practice for mechanically ventilated adults. The supporting meta-analysis found lower VAP rates with this intervention but no demonstrated difference in duration of mechanical ventilation or mortality, so head-of-bed elevation should be used as one component of a broader prevention strategy rather than as a stand-alone substitute for other recommended practices. CDC's February 25, 2026 pneumonia guideline index identifies this SHEA/IDSA guidance as current VAP-prevention guidance.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: For mechanically ventilated adults without a contraindication, use 30–45-degree head-of-bed elevation as one component of VAP-prevention care.

audit_findings_append.finding: The original concept was supported but distractor wording was uneven. The revised item tests the recommended 30–45-degree positioning without overstating mortality or ventilation-duration benefit.

option_audit.A: Correct. The current acute-care prevention guidance lists 30–45-degree head-of-bed elevation as an essential practice for ventilated adults.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. The guidance recommends elevation rather than routine supine positioning when not contraindicated.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. Head-of-bed elevation is recommended as prevention, not only after VAP develops.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. It is one element of a broader ventilator-prevention strategy and does not replace other recommended practices.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. A alone matches the current prevention recommendation without overclaiming the evidence.
cueing_check: All four choices are positioning/prevention actions of comparable length and specificity; no absolute-word or unique-length cue identifies A.
